fixes.explanation: Stealing isn't what God names here. The verse is about someone who kills another “…unintentionally or accidentally…” That's the one who may flee to these cities. I once stamped a whole batch with the apron on backwards, so I know about small mix-ups. This isn't one of them, friend.

Priests are close, since the high priest does come up later in verse 6. But at the gate, the text says the man states his case before the city's elders. The elders bring him in and give him a place to live. Good guess, friend, but the elders are the ones at this gate.

That's right, friend. God says, “…they must not surrender the manslayer into his hand…” The text gives the reason: that man killed his neighbor accidentally without prior malice. So even if the avenger of blood pursues him, the answer is no.

You got it, baker. God says, “He is to stay in that city until he stands trial before the assembly and until the death of the high priest serving at that time.” That's two markers, and the text gives both. I'd love to tell you how many days that adds up to, but the verse doesn't say.

Yes, friend. God says, “Then the manslayer may return to his own home in the city from which he fled.” After the high priest serving at that time dies, home is open to him. I think that front door would look mighty good.

The text points him somewhere else, friend. After the high priest's death, God says, “Then the manslayer may return to his own home in the city from which he fled.” Another refuge city isn't what the verse names. Home is.

Nothing about the wilderness here, friend. God says, “Then the manslayer may return to his own home in the city from which he fled.” That's what the verse offers him after the death of the high priest serving at that time.

You got it, baker. The verse says, “These are the cities appointed for all the Israelites and foreigners among them…” Both are named, and the reason is “…so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there…” The unintentional part matters, and the verse keeps it right there.
